title: Block Proposer Blob Field Element Range Validation: Delegated to C-KZG Library

abstract_interpretation.summary: The block proposer path does not perform explicit Go-level range checking on blob field elements before including blobs in blocks. The CL does not generate blobs; it receives them from the EL via the engine API. The ELMemPoolRequirements is explicitly empty, and blob KZG proof verification against the EL is performed via kzg.VerifyBlobKZGProofBatch (pre-Fulu) and kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatchFromBlobData (Fulu). Both internally call blob_to_polynomial which unconditionally invokes bytes_to_bls_field for each of the 4096 field elements. bytes_to_bls_field calls blst_scalar_fr_check, which returns C_KZG_BADARGS if any byte sequence encodes a value >= BLS_MODULUS.
findings: ELMemPoolRequirements is empty (beacon-chain/verification/blob.go:77): no explicit CL-layer requirement enforced for blobs from EL mempool.

In the block proposal validation path (handlers.go:validateBlobs), kzg.VerifyBlobKZGProofBatch and kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatchFromBlobData are called, which both eventually call blob_to_polynomial in the C-KZG library.
blob_to_polynomial (c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/eip4844/blob.c:35) iterates all FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB elements and calls bytes_to_bls_field for each.
bytes_to_bls_field (c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/common/bytes.c:64) calls blst_scalar_fr_check and returns C_KZG_BADARGS if the value is out-of-range.
The error propagates as ErrBadArgs through ckzg4844.VerifyBlobKZGProofBatch -> kzg.VerifyBlobKZGProofBatch -> handlers.go:validateBlobs, causing block proposal to fail.

For the proposer path, blocks are built from EL payloads and cell proofs provided by the EL (trusted). If the EL is compromised or produces invalid blobs, the CL's KZG verification catches it via the C library range check.
abstract_interpretation.verdict: PASS - Range validation is enforced by the C-KZG library during the KZG proof verification step that is mandatory in the block proposal validation path.

symbolic_execution.summary: Trace: actor-block-proposer -> handlers.go:validateBlobs -> kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatchFromBlobData (Fulu) -> ComputeCells -> ckzg4844.ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs -> C blob_to_polynomial -> bytes_to_bls_field(blst_scalar_fr_check). If any field element byte is >= BLS_MODULUS, bytes_to_bls_field returns C_KZG_BADARGS, ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs returns error, VerifyCellKZGProofBatchFromBlobData returns error, validateBlobs returns error, ProposeBeaconBlock fails.
findings: Pre-Fulu path: kzg.VerifyBlobKZGProofBatch -> crate-crypto go-kzg-4844 VerifyBlobKZGProofBatch calls DeserializeBlob -> SetBytesCanonical (canonical range check). Error path terminates block proposal.

Fulu path: kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatchFromBlobData calls ComputeCells which calls ckzg4844.ComputeCells -> C compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs -> blob_to_polynomial -> bytes_to_bls_field. Out-of-range value returns error.
The range check is identical across both code paths: the C library checks blst_scalar_fr_check, the Go library checks SetBytesCanonical.
Note: In the Fulu path, ComputeCells is called on the blobs from the EL. If any blob byte is >= BLS_MODULUS, this call fails before any cells are computed, preventing inclusion of invalid blobs.
symbolic_execution.verdict: PASS - Symbolic execution confirms all reachable code paths from actor-block-proposer result in early abort when field element range is violated.

invariant_proving.summary: Invariant: For all blobs b included in a block, for all field elements f in b, f < BLS_MODULUS. This invariant is proven by the C-KZG library's blob_to_polynomial function which is called as part of every blob-related KZG operation before the blob is accepted.
findings: Invariant is enforced by the C library at the point of deserialization (blob_to_polynomial -> bytes_to_bls_field -> blst_scalar_fr_check).
The invariant is not explicitly enforced at the Go layer before calling the C library, but the C library guarantees it through error returns.
ELMemPoolRequirements being empty means the CL trusts the EL for mempool blobs, but the KZG proof verification step in validateBlobs acts as the final gate before block inclusion.
Invariant holds: a proposer cannot include a blob with out-of-range field elements because validateBlobs would fail, preventing block proposal.
invariant_proving.verdict: PROVEN - The field element range invariant is enforced by the C-KZG library in the block proposal validation pipeline.

evidence: Key code references: (1) beacon-chain/verification/blob.go:77: ELMemPoolRequirements is empty. (2) beacon-chain/rpc/eth/beacon/handlers.go:1069-1104: validateBlobs calls kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatchFromBlobData (Fulu) or kzg.VerifyBlobKZGProofBatch (pre-Fulu). (3) beacon-chain/blockchain/kzg/validation.go:105-167: VerifyCellKZGProofBatchFromBlobData calls ComputeCells which calls ckzg4844.ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs. (4) c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/eip4844/blob.c:35-40: blob_to_polynomial calls bytes_to_bls_field for each field element. (5) c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/common/bytes.c:64-70: bytes_to_bls_field calls blst_scalar_fr_check, returns C_KZG_BADARGS if out of range. (6) crate-crypto/go-kzg-4844@v1.1.0/serialization.go:110-119: DeserializeBlob calls SetBytesCanonical which enforces canonical range. The EL->CL trust relationship does not bypass the KZG range check because validateBlobs is always called.
recommendation: No code change required. The existing delegation to the C-KZG library correctly enforces field element range validation for all blobs before block inclusion. Consider adding a comment in validateBlobs (handlers.go) documenting that the C-KZG library enforces the BLS_MODULUS range constraint implicitly as part of blob_to_polynomial.

title: Validator Node Data Availability Verification: Field Element Range Check Enforced via C-KZG and Go-KZG Libraries

abstract_interpretation.summary: The validator node data availability verification path uses GossipDataColumnSidecarRequirements for P2P gossip data columns and GossipBlobSidecarRequirements for blob sidecars. Both require RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified, which calls verifyDataColumnsCommitment -> peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> C verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch. Inside that C function, compute_commitment_to_aggregated_interpolation_poly calls bytes_to_bls_field for every field element of every cell. Out-of-range values produce C_KZG_BADARGS, which is returned as ErrBadArgs through all layers.
findings: verification/data_column.go:26-39: GossipDataColumnSidecarRequirements includes RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified at position 11.
verification/data_column.go:389-405: SidecarKzgProofVerified calls dv.verifyDataColumnsCommitment(dv.dataColumns).
verification/initializer.go: verifyDataColumnsCommitment is initialized to peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs.
beacon-chain/core/peerdas/p2p_interface.go:61-93: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs calls kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch.
beacon-chain/blockchain/kzg/kzg.go:98-106: VerifyCellKZGProofBatch calls ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch.
c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/eip7594/eip7594.c:656-683: compute_commitment_to_aggregated_interpolation_poly calls bytes_to_bls_field for each cell field element.
c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/common/bytes.c:64-70: bytes_to_bls_field calls blst_scalar_fr_check, returns C_KZG_BADARGS if out of range.

For blob sidecars on gossip: verification/blob.go:276-283: SidecarKzgProofVerified calls bv.verifyBlobCommitment which is set to kzg.Verify, which uses crate-crypto go-kzg-4844 VerifyBlobKZGProof -> DeserializeBlob -> SetBytesCanonical (canonical range check).
abstract_interpretation.verdict: PASS - Both data column sidecar and blob sidecar verification paths enforce field element range checks via their respective KZG libraries.

symbolic_execution.summary: Data column gossip path: P2P message -> sync/data_column_sidecars.go -> validateWithKzgBatchVerifier -> verifyKzgBatch -> peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> C verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch -> compute_commitment_to_aggregated_interpolation_poly -> bytes_to_bls_field (range check). If range check fails: C_KZG_BADARGS -> ErrBadArgs -> error returned -> ValidationReject (P2P message rejected).
findings: The gossip path in sync/batch_verifier.go:157-214 uses validateWithKzgBatchVerifier -> verifyKzgBatch. Batch failure triggers fallback to validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg (line 186) which also calls peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs.
Both batch and unbatched paths reach the same C library range check.
For init-sync path: InitsyncBlobSidecarRequirements includes RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified, so range check is enforced there too.
For ByRange/ByRoot RPC data column requests: ByRangeRequestDataColumnSidecarRequirements and ByRootRequestDataColumnSidecarRequirements both include RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified.
ELMemPoolRequirements is empty but this applies only to blobs stored from EL mempool, not to P2P data availability verification.
symbolic_execution.verdict: PASS - All validator node data availability verification paths enforce field element range checks through the C-KZG or Go-KZG library.

invariant_proving.summary: Invariant: For all data column sidecars and blob sidecars accepted by the validator node, all cell/blob field elements satisfy f < BLS_MODULUS. This invariant is proved by the mandatory RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified requirement in all requirement sets used for P2P reception and RPC reception.
findings: RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified is present in GossipDataColumnSidecarRequirements, ByRangeRequestDataColumnSidecarRequirements, ByRootRequestDataColumnSidecarRequirements, GossipBlobSidecarRequirements, InitsyncBlobSidecarRequirements, SpectestDataColumnSidecarRequirements.
The only exception is ELMemPoolRequirements (empty), but this path covers blobs provided by the trusted EL, not P2P data availability.
The range check is enforced consistently across both C-KZG (for cells) and Go-KZG (for blobs): C blst_scalar_fr_check vs Go SetBytesCanonical - both reject values >= BLS_MODULUS.
Invariant holds across all external-facing data availability verification entry points.
invariant_proving.verdict: PROVEN - The field element range invariant is enforced in all validator node data availability verification paths.

evidence: Key code references: (1) beacon-chain/verification/data_column.go:26-39: GossipDataColumnSidecarRequirements includes RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified. (2) beacon-chain/verification/data_column.go:389-405: SidecarKzgProofVerified calls verifyDataColumnsCommitment. (3) beacon-chain/sync/batch_verifier.go:194-214: verifyKzgBatch calls peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs. (4) beacon-chain/core/peerdas/p2p_interface.go:61-93: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs calls kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. (5) c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/eip7594/eip7594.c:656-683: bytes_to_bls_field called for each cell field element in compute_commitment_to_aggregated_interpolation_poly. (6) c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/common/bytes.c:64-70: bytes_to_bls_field range check with blst_scalar_fr_check.
recommendation: No code change required. The field element range validation is consistently enforced by the underlying KZG libraries across all data availability verification paths. Consider documenting in the codebase that the C-KZG library performs implicit range validation as part of cell deserialization.

title: Falsification Test: Out-of-Range Blob Bytes Cannot Produce Cells That Pass verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch

abstract_interpretation.summary: The test hypothesis - that out-of-range blob bytes (>= BLS_MODULUS) could produce cells that pass verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch - is falsified by the C-KZG implementation. When verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch is called with cells derived from out-of-range blobs, the C library calls bytes_to_bls_field for each cell field element inside compute_commitment_to_aggregated_interpolation_poly. If any field element is out of range, C_KZG_BADARGS is returned, causing the verification to fail with an error (not return false), rather than silently applying modular reduction.
findings: c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/common/bytes.c:64-70: bytes_to_bls_field explicitly calls blst_scalar_fr_check and returns C_KZG_BADARGS (an error) if the check fails. This is distinct from hash_to_bls_field (bytes.c:123-127) which applies modular reduction without checking.

bytes_to_bls_field vs hash_to_bls_field distinction: bytes_to_bls_field is used for deserialization of untrusted input (blob field elements, cell field elements); hash_to_bls_field is used for hash outputs (Fiat-Shamir challenge). Only the deserialization path validates range.
In verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (eip7594.c:821-), compute_commitment_to_aggregated_interpolation_poly is called which calls bytes_to_bls_field for each field element of each cell (eip7594.c:666-669).
If C_KZG_BADARGS is returned from bytes_to_bls_field, the function jumps to the out: label and returns C_KZG_BADARGS to Go, which becomes ErrBadArgs.
The Go layer returns (false, ErrBadArgs) from ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch when ret != C_KZG_OK (main.go:522-524).
In peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs: if err != nil, the error is wrapped and returned (p2p_interface.go:84-86). The cell sidecar is rejected.
There is no path where out-of-range cell bytes would pass the verification silently through modular reduction.
abstract_interpretation.verdict: FALSIFIED - The hypothesis is false. Out-of-range blob/cell bytes cause an explicit error return (C_KZG_BADARGS), not silent acceptance or modular reduction.

symbolic_execution.summary: Concrete attack scenario: Attacker crafts a cell with field element bytes f where f >= BLS_MODULUS. Attacker sends this as a data column sidecar via P2P gossip. In verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch -> compute_commitment_to_aggregated_interpolation_poly, bytes_to_bls_field(f) is called. blst_scalar_fr_check(f) returns false. bytes_to_bls_field returns C_KZG_BADARGS. verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch returns C_KZG_BADARGS. Go returns (false, ErrBadArgs). peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs returns error. P2P validation rejects the sidecar.
findings: Distinct behavior between bytes_to_bls_field (range-checked, errors on violation) and hash_to_bls_field (modular reduction, no error) is clearly intentional in the C-KZG design.

The C-KZG source comment on bytes_to_bls_field (bytes.c:58-63) explicitly states: 'Convert untrusted bytes to a trusted and validated BLS scalar field element.' The word 'trusted and validated' confirms the intent to reject out-of-range values.
The cell deserialization inside verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch uses bytes_to_bls_field (the validated version), not hash_to_bls_field.
Similarly, blob_to_polynomial (blob.c:35-40) uses bytes_to_bls_field for blob deserialization.

No code path within the C library applies silent modular reduction to externally-supplied field element bytes. Silent reduction is only applied to hash outputs (hash_to_bls_field, blst_fr_from_scalar).
symbolic_execution.verdict: FALSIFIED - Symbolic execution confirms the attack path is blocked. C_KZG_BADARGS propagates as an error, preventing any out-of-range field element from entering the cryptographic computation.

invariant_proving.summary: Invariant: bytes_to_bls_field(b) succeeds only if b represents a value in [0, BLS_MODULUS - 1]. This invariant is proven by the blst_scalar_fr_check call in bytes_to_bls_field. An invariant that would allow out-of-range values to pass verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch cannot be constructed because the range check is a prerequisite for any arithmetic on the field element.
findings: blst_scalar_fr_check is a BLST library function that checks whether a scalar is in the scalar field (i.e., < BLS_MODULUS). It is called unconditionally in bytes_to_bls_field.
The C-KZG library consistently uses bytes_to_bls_field (not hash_to_bls_field) for all untrusted cell and blob field element deserialization paths.
The invariant is also enforced in the recovery path: recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs -> cell deserialization at eip7594.c:248 uses bytes_to_bls_field.
The crate-crypto/go-kzg-4844 library enforces the same invariant via SetBytesCanonical and ReduceCanonicalBigEndian for blob field elements.
Both libraries used in Prysm enforce the field element range invariant consistently.
invariant_proving.verdict: PROVEN - The invariant that out-of-range field element bytes are rejected is provably enforced by blst_scalar_fr_check in bytes_to_bls_field, called for all untrusted field element deserialization.

evidence: Critical code references: (1) c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/common/bytes.c:64-70: bytes_to_bls_field: 'blst_scalar_from_bendian(&tmp, b->bytes); if (!blst_scalar_fr_check(&tmp)) return C_KZG_BADARGS; blst_fr_from_scalar(out, &tmp);' - explicit range validation. (2) c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/common/bytes.c:123-127: hash_to_bls_field: 'blst_scalar_from_bendian(&tmp, b->bytes); blst_fr_from_scalar(out, &tmp);' - NO range check, for hash outputs only. (3) c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/eip7594/eip7594.c:666-669: compute_commitment_to_aggregated_interpolation_poly calls bytes_to_bls_field (validated version). (4) c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/eip4844/blob.c:35-40: blob_to_polynomial calls bytes_to_bls_field for every blob field element. (5) c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/bindings/go/main.go:508-524: Go binding returns (false, ErrBadArgs) when C library returns non-OK.
recommendation: No action required. The C-KZG library correctly rejects out-of-range field elements with an explicit error. The design is correct: bytes_to_bls_field for untrusted input (enforces range), hash_to_bls_field for hash outputs (applies reduction). This matches the Ethereum consensus spec's bytes_to_bls_field specification which also rejects non-canonical values.

title: Implementation Consistency: Both KZG Libraries Used in Prysm Enforce Consistent Field Element Range Checking

abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm uses two KZG libraries: (1) crate-crypto/go-kzg-4844 (Go pure implementation, for blob sidecar verification via kzg.Verify) and (2) ethereum/c-kzg-4844/v2 (C library bindings, for cell KZG proof batch verification and Fulu operations). Both libraries implement the bytes_to_bls_field specification consistently by rejecting values >= BLS_MODULUS with an error. The rejection behavior is consistent: both return an error (not a boolean false), causing callers to propagate the error up the stack.
findings: Path 1 (blob sidecars, pre-Fulu): beacon-chain/blockchain/kzg/validation.go:Verify -> crate-crypto go-kzg-4844 VerifyBlobKZGProof -> DeserializeBlob (serialization.go:110-119) -> SetBytesCanonical -> ReduceCanonicalBigEndian (canonical range check). ErrNonCanonicalScalar returned on violation.

Path 2 (blob sidecars batch, pre-Fulu): kzg.VerifyBlobKZGProofBatch (validation.go) can use either crate-crypto (single blob) or c-kzg-4844 (batch). c-kzg-4844 VerifyBlobKZGProofBatch calls blob_to_polynomial -> bytes_to_bls_field. Consistent range rejection.
Path 3 (data column cells, Fulu): kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> C verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch -> bytes_to_bls_field. Consistent rejection.
Path 4 (recovery, Fulu): kzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs -> ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs -> C recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs -> bytes_to_bls_field (eip7594.c:248). Consistent rejection.

Path 5 (commitment computation, proposer): kzg.BlobToKZGCommitment -> kzg4844.BlobToCommitment (go-ethereum) or kzg.ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs -> ckzg4844.ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs -> blob_to_polynomial -> bytes_to_bls_field. Consistent rejection.
Both libraries consistently return an error on range violation, not boolean false. This is correct behavior per the spec: bytes_to_bls_field should assert the value is canonical.
abstract_interpretation.verdict: CONSISTENT - All bytes_to_bls_field implementations across both KZG libraries used in Prysm use consistent canonical range checking with error return on violation.

symbolic_execution.summary: Comparison of range check mechanisms: C-KZG (blst_scalar_fr_check in bytes_to_bls_field) vs Go-KZG (SetBytesCanonical / ReduceCanonicalBigEndian in DeserializeBlob/DeserializeScalar). Both implement the same semantic: compare the input byte sequence as a big-endian integer against the BLS12-381 scalar field modulus and return an error if the value is not in [0, p-1].
findings: blst_scalar_fr_check in BLST library performs a lexicographic comparison of the scalar bytes against the modulus bytes in big-endian form and returns false if the value is out of range.
gnark-crypto's ReduceCanonicalBigEndian (used by crate-crypto/go-kzg-4844) performs the same check: reads the bytes as a big-endian integer and checks if it is less than the field modulus.
Both checks reject the point at value == BLS_MODULUS (not just > BLS_MODULUS), consistent with the spec requiring values in [0, p-1].
No divergence found between the two library implementations for out-of-range inputs. Both reject with an error.
The go-ethereum kzg4844 library (used in BlobToKZGCommitment via kzg4844.BlobToCommitment) also uses a BLST-based implementation with the same range semantics.
symbolic_execution.verdict: CONSISTENT - Symbolic execution confirms that all three underlying KZG libraries (c-kzg-4844, go-kzg-4844, go-ethereum kzg4844) implement consistent canonical range checking for bytes_to_bls_field.

invariant_proving.summary: Consistency invariant: For all deserialization functions f in {bytes_to_bls_field_c, DeserializeBlob_go, DeserializeScalar_go}, f(b) is a well-formed field element if and only if b represents a value in [0, BLS_MODULUS - 1]. All three implementations satisfy this invariant.
findings: c-kzg-4844 bytes_to_bls_field: uses BLST blst_scalar_fr_check. Proven correct by BLST library design and BLS12-381 curve parameters.
crate-crypto go-kzg-4844 DeserializeBlob/DeserializeScalar: uses SetBytesCanonical / ReduceCanonicalBigEndian from gnark-crypto. Documented as returning ErrNonCanonicalScalar for out-of-range values.
go-ethereum kzg4844 uses BLST internally for the same BLS12-381 scalar field.
The consistency invariant holds: no implementation silently applies modular reduction to untrusted deserialized field elements.
The distinction between trusted (hash output, apply modular reduction) vs untrusted (external input, range-check and reject) is consistent across all implementations.
invariant_proving.verdict: PROVEN - The field element range consistency invariant holds across all KZG library implementations used in Prysm.

evidence: Key evidence: (1) c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/common/bytes.c:58-70: bytes_to_bls_field comment 'Convert untrusted bytes to a trusted and validated BLS scalar field element' - uses blst_scalar_fr_check, returns C_KZG_BADARGS. (2) crate-crypto/go-kzg-4844@v1.1.0/serialization.go:121-132: DeserializeScalar comment 'Returns an error if the scalar is not in the range [0, p-1] (inclusive)' - uses ReduceCanonicalBigEndian. (3) crate-crypto/go-kzg-4844@v1.1.0/serialization.go:107-119: DeserializeBlob calls SetBytesCanonical for each scalar. (4) c-kzg-4844/v2@v2.1.1/src/common/bytes.c:123-127: hash_to_bls_field does NOT call blst_scalar_fr_check (no range check for hash outputs - intentional design choice). (5) All three libraries: go-ethereum kzg4844, crate-crypto go-kzg-4844, and ethereum c-kzg-4844 use BLST or gnark-crypto with the same BLS12-381 scalar field modulus.
recommendation: No action required. The implementation is consistent across all KZG libraries. The auditor should note that the two distinct functions bytes_to_bls_field (range-checked) and hash_to_bls_field (modular reduction) are intentional and correct by design: external inputs must be canonical, hash outputs are always in-range by the hash's uniform distribution properties.

title: Downstream Protection: Error Propagation from bytes_to_bls_field Through Full KZG Pipeline is Correct

abstract_interpretation.summary: The error propagation chain from bytes_to_bls_field through the full KZG pipeline is correctly implemented. When bytes_to_bls_field returns C_KZG_BADARGS, all downstream operations are aborted via goto out patterns and error returns. The Go binding correctly translates C_KZG_BADARGS to ErrBadArgs. All Go callers check errors and propagate them to their callers without swallowing them. The final result is that the P2P message or block proposal that triggered the operation is rejected with an appropriate error.
findings: C layer error propagation: bytes_to_bls_field returns C_KZG_BADARGS -> all callers (blob_to_polynomial, compute_commitment_to_aggregated_interpolation_poly) use 'if (ret != C_KZG_OK) goto out;' or 'if (ret != C_KZG_OK) return ret;' patterns, correctly aborting all downstream operations.
Go binding (main.go:520-524): 'if ret != C.C_KZG_OK { return false, makeErrorFromRet(ret) }' - returns (false, ErrBadArgs) instead of (false, nil).
peerdas/p2p_interface.go:83-86: 'if err != nil { return errors.Wrap(err, "verify cell KZG proof batch") }' - error wrapped and returned, no swallowing.

sync/batch_verifier.go:204-208: 'err := peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs(allDataColumns); if err != nil { verificationErr = errors.Wrap(...) }' - error set, propagated to all verifiers in batch.
sync/batch_verifier.go:210-213: Each verifier in the batch receives verificationErr via resChan, triggering fallback to unbatched verification.

sync/batch_verifier.go:183-191: validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg: 'if err := peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs(columns); err != nil { return pubsub.ValidationReject, err }' - ValidationReject on error.
verification/data_column.go:389-404: SidecarKzgProofVerified returns columnErrBuilder(errors.Wrap(err, ...)) on error.
No code path was found where the error from bytes_to_bls_field is swallowed or where execution continues after a range check failure.
abstract_interpretation.verdict: CORRECT - Error propagation from bytes_to_bls_field is correctly implemented. All downstream operations are aborted when a range check fails.

symbolic_execution.summary: Full error propagation trace for out-of-range field element in a cell: bytes_to_bls_field(f) [C_KZG_BADARGS] -> compute_commitment_to_aggregated_interpolation_poly returns C_KZG_BADARGS [via goto out] -> verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch returns C_KZG_BADARGS [via goto out] -> ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch returns (false, ErrBadArgs) -> kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch returns (false, ErrBadArgs) -> peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs returns error -> verifyKzgBatch sets verificationErr -> resChan receives error -> validateWithKzgBatchVerifier receives error -> fallback to validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg -> ValidationReject.
